scope: Read-only review of the named R12 resource audit script and corrected public integration notes. No generator, product test, resource, source, Git or runtime mutation was performed.

checks.evidence: The script only traverses and reads the supplied root/fixture, parses in memory, constructs validators/registries and prints JSON. Static inspection found no filesystem mutation calls; it does not import the project, invoke subprocesses, Git or network.

The ten exact R12 filenames, profile path, directory set and no-symlink/no-extra-file set are enforced. Each resource/profile must decode as UTF-8, reject duplicate keys/floats/constants, reproduce json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False) plus one LF, and pass Draft 2020-12 root metadata checks.

Every schema $ref is checked against the ten exact $ids and JSON Pointer lookup; nested ids, anchors and dynamic/recursive references are rejected. The explicit Registry denies undeclared retrieval. This matches R12, while not claiming semantic replay.

All R12 LIMITS/ADMISSION values, exact profile shape, sorted ten-row inventory, positive sizes and schema-byte hashes are checked. The profile SHA-256 is computed and matched to the fixture. No independent expected profile/schema hash manifest is supplied, so this cannot establish the R12 trust root by itself.
The extended Draft validator uses type(value) is int and rejects True, 1.0 and an int subclass; the same strict validator validates the profile definition and every positive instance.

With a fixture, it requires the closed top-level/case shapes, 264 unique ASCII names in sorted order, all nine instance-schema titles and successful strict validation of every instance. It does not independently prove the prepared category inventory or fixture canonical byte formatting.

The notes correctly restore bundle.json as a direct slot and byte-identical raw manifest copy, use SHA-256(logical ASCII target path) path keys, keep only handoff JSON files with source_body_path pointing to retained objects, use exact handoffs spelling, separate the fourteen-path resource increment from later public code, and require retained-I/O/adversarial tests. These agree with R4 lines 65-149, R7 lines 249-319 and R9 lines 1-12/122-189.

required_followups.finding: Freeze an external manifest of the reviewed eleven resource bytes and compare against it; otherwise mutually replaced profile/schema bytes with internally consistent inventory hashes could pass this script.

All acceptance checks use assert. Running with python -O disables them and can overclaim success. Pin a non-optimized interpreter or convert checks to explicit exceptions before treating output as acceptance.

Keep nested closed-shape negatives, unknown/omitted fields, profile-bound fixture inventory/category coverage and wheel byte parity in the separate resource tests; this script must remain bounded and must not be cited as proving them.

The exact-tree walk does not explicitly reject a symlink supplied as the root itself. The generator contract supplies an absent fresh root; if this audit is reused independently, add a root is_dir/non-symlink check.

limitations: No resource root or fixture was executed because none was supplied and product tests were out of scope.
This is a bounded audit review, not resource generation or public CODE acceptance.
